facts.text: In 1925, the U.S. Post Office renamed the town Gustavus after Point Gustavus at the mouth of Glacier Bay, replacing the earlier name Strawberry Point.
Gustavus sits on an outwash plain formed by glaciers that once filled Glacier Bay, and the Salmon River splits the town, crossing a bridge into the park.
The first permanent homestead in Gustavus was established in 1917 when Abraham Lincoln Parker moved his family to Strawberry Point, and many residents descend from those early settlers.
Gustavus is situated in the ancestral homeland of the Huna Tlingit, and the town honors this heritage through its Visitor Association and historical archives.
Gustavus enjoys a temperate rainforest climate, with summer temperatures ranging from 11 to 17 °C and winter lows around –3 °C, thanks to its coastal location.
Coho salmon and Dolly Varden are commonly caught in the Salmon River, which is tidal within the city limits and supports a vibrant fishing culture.
